== Biography ==
=== Current Wilson father assessment — 31 October 2026 ===
The inspected FamilySearch marriage index expressly labels Wilson A. Glasgow as Robert Glasgow’s son in the 7 November 1844 Chambers County, Alabama marriage to Sealy Ann Bohanan. Wilson-405’s unusual full given name/initial and named bride identify the indexed groom. The original 1850 Floyd County census puts Robert Glasgow’s household 644 immediately before Wilson A. Glasgow’s household 645, continuing across two pages. Both men are recorded as born in South Carolina; Wilson is 26 and his Ceily A., 24, born Alabama, and three named children agree with the maintained Wilson/Cecilia family. The named parent role comes from the marriage index; the census identifies the compatible Robert account and family context without stating kinship. Together these support the complete Wilson-405 to Robert-2298 father identification at 93% subjective confidence, beyond the former 49% tree-attribution assessment.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QKMB-QG6X Alabama County Marriages, Robert Glasgow in the Wilson A. Glasgow/Sealy Ann Bohanan entry, 7 November 1844]. Provider index explicitly labels Robert as father; original unavailable online. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-6WSS-9MK Original 1850 census, Robert household 644]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-6WSS-M53 continuation and Wilson household 645], Floyd County, Georgia, subdivision 30. Index and census originals inspected 31 October 2026.</ref>

The marriage is an inspected provider index, not an inspected original: DGS 007251125 image 999 was explicitly unavailable online in the signed-in viewer. An index error remains possible. The census has no relationship column and consecutive enumeration numbers do not themselves prove fatherhood or shared property. Robert’s age is indexed 50, while the handwritten last digit can be read 50/57; no exact birth-year correction follows. The two census pages are one household continuation, not independent parentage witnesses. Same existing father retained; no new attachment, mother, spouse, vital field or upstream confidence change.

This supersedes the earlier 49% Possible father assessment for [[Glasgow-405]] → [[Glasgow-2298]], retained below as dated history. It does not attach a new father or assess [[Bohannon-337]] anew.

Robert Glasgow was born about 1800 in South Carolina, probably a son of [[Glasgow-1982|Wilson Crossier Glasgow]]. Wilson's real-estate packet index lists Robert with widow Mary and the seven-person child group matching the seven shares in Mary's will.<ref name="WilsonEstate">Newberry County, South Carolina, real-estate packet 1-13, estate of Wilson Glasgow; [https://genealogytrails.com/scar/newberry/realestate.html index], listing Mary, Robert, Ruth, Naomi, Matilda, Hiram, Almina and Maria.</ref> This supports Wilson as Robert’s probable father, assessed at 84%; the parties’ exact relationships still require checking against the original packet. The index does not by itself explicitly identify [[McCracken-3711|Mary McCracken]] as Robert's mother, so that relationship remains separately assessed.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1982]] is assessed at 84% (probable). Wilson’s real-estate packet index lists widow Mary with Robert among the apparent seven-child group. This is a specific estate-family context fitting Robert-2298’s generation and Newberry setting, stronger than a bare tree link. Mary’s 1837 will does not itself name this Robert.

Probable84%; the uninspected original packet must establish the parties’ exact roles. The estate index is not a literal father clause.

Next useful test: Read packet1–13 for Robert’s stated relationship to Wilson and Mary.

Source basis already held: [https://www.genealogytrails.com/scar/newberry/realestate.html Newberry real-estate packet index, Wilson Glasgow, packet1–13; Mary and Robert among listed parties]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.


Robert was born in Newberry, South Carolina, and was buried in Gordon County, Georgia. The 1850 census shows him born in South Carolina and living in Floyd County, Georgia. 

Ages and birthplaces from the 1850 census suggest that the family moved from South Carolina to Georgia sometime between 1823 and 1830.

The 1850 census showing Robert's household spans two pages. It shows three women named Elizabeth living in the household, ages 55, 27, and 15.  Elizabeth age 55 is presumably John's wife. Elizabeth age 27 was born in South Carolina and Elizabeth L age 15 was born in Georgia. One of the Elizabeths may have been a niece or other relative rather than a daughter. 

The 1850 census also shows that the adjacent dwelling was occupied by the [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-405 Wilson] and [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Bohannon-337 Cecilia] Glasgow and their three children.
